newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Slow going after stellar start.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Slow going after stellar start.

text.p: Asian debt markets were quiet on Tuesday after a frenetic start to the week.
Further details emerged on Hong Kong semiconductor manufacturer QPL International's US$100 million floating rate note issue.
The notes are due 2002 but can be put after three years. The paper also can be called at par on coupon dates after the third anniversary.
The issue was launched at par to float at 145 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate. With fees, the all-in return to top tier participants is 168 basis points.
QTL International subsidiaries ASAT Ltd and QPL Ltd are guarantors for the issue.
Sumitomo Finance Asia and Standard Chartered Bank are arrangers.
Bankers were generally positive on the issue because it offers a high coupon and a rare opportunity to take exposure to a Hong Kong company.
"It looks quite generous and just based on demand for Hong Kong corporates the issue should do well. But I wouldn't expect the issue to be very liquid," said a syndicate manager at a European bank.
A US$78 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue for Bank Dagang Nasional Indonesia is expected to be launched imminently.
Bankgesselschaft Berlin, BZW Asia, Indover Bank, ING Barings and NatWest Markets are arrangers.
Meanwhile, bankers continue to mull the recent Philippine bank issues.
Philippine National Bank's three-year US$125 million FRCD launched on Monday was deemed tightly priced, even considering the narrowing trend in spreads.

"PNB is not one of the best bank credits in the Philippines, despite its name, and the issue doesn't reflect as good a value as some of the other bank issues that are out," said the European bank syndicate manager.
"I prefer China Banking Corp," said another banker, adding that he was keen on Coconut Bank's three-year FRCD but not the five-year paper.
China Banking Corp's three-year US$60 million FRCD pays an all-in of 91 basis points, while United Coconut Planters Bank is offering 85 basis points for its three-year tranche.
Bankers said they still favor three-year Philippine bank paper over five-year issues, despite an improving view of the country's outlook. -- Andrea Ricci (852) 2843-6371 fax (852) 2845-0636
